AUTORES: N. Prieto; Ó. López-Campos; W. Barragán-Hernández; B. Schmidt
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, Lacombe Research and Development Centre, University of Guelph, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This study compared air-frying with three conventional cooking methods (broiling, grilling, and pan-frying) and evaluated their effects on colour, fat content and palatability of beef patties (n=288 in total) with different fat levels (medium, lean and extra-lean; 96 of each fatness level). Regardless of fat level, cooking method affected all colour parameters ( P <0.001): pan-frying and broiling produced the highest L * (37.5 and 39.4 ± 0.62, respectively), pan-frying and air-frying the highest a* (8.32 and 8.73 ± 0.134, respectively), and pan-frying the highest b * (16.1 ± 0.28), whereas grilling produced lower colour values. Across all fat levels, air-frying and broiling reduced cooking time by more than 6% and 26%, respectively, but increased cooking losses by 14%, whereas grilling and pan-frying produced higher beef flavour intensity (+0.31 to +0.69 units) and juiciness (+0.58 to +1.31 units) ( P <0.001). Fat level × cooking method interactions influenced tenderness ( P <0.01) and fat content ( P <0.001), with grilling and/or pan-frying enhancing initial and/or overall tenderness in lean and extra-lean patties (+0.42 to +0.81 units), and air-frying and broiling reducing fat content in medium (-0.84 to -1.06%) and lean (-0.63 to -1.25%) patties. Overall, grilling and pan-frying provided superior sensory characteristics, while broiling and air-frying were more effective at reducing fat content in medium and lean patties. These findings highlight the trade-off between fat reduction and eating quality, providing practical guidance for selecting cooking methods. Future research should evaluate the applicability of these findings to fresh or thawed patties and determine whether the observed differences translate into consumer acceptance.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Multisensor, Multitemporal Forage Dataset: Megathyrsus maximus cv. Mombasa under Tropical Silvopastoral Conditions (Wet and Dry Seasons, Colombian Caribbean) Overview This dataset comprises 400 structured observations of individual Megathyrsus maximus cv. Mombasa tussocks collected at the AGROSAVIA Turipaná Research Centre (Cereté, Córdoba, Colombia; 8°53′N, 75°49′W) during two contrasting climatic periods: Wet season: August 16 – September 13, 2024 Dry season: March 7 – April 4, 2025 Forty georeferenced tussocks were monitored under two light conditions: 19 shaded tussocks and 21 full-sun tussocks. Measurements were acquired every 5 days at regrowth days 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35, generating 200 observations per season (95 shaded and 105 full-sun observations per season). The dataset integrates proximal sensing, RGB imaging, UAV multispectral imagery, Sentinel-2 satellite products, environmental variables, and destructive laboratory measurements to characterize forage growth dynamics, canopy spectral response, biomass accumulation, and nutritional quality under tropical silvopastoral conditions. Documentation Files This repository includes two documentation files in addition to the master dataset: Data_Dictionary_BD_Forage2Season.xlsx — a complete, column-by-column dictionary of all 107 variables in the Dataset-Wet-Dry sheet, specifying variable name, description, category, data type, unit/format, source/origin, and processing level (Raw vs. Derived, including file-reference columns). It also documents the missing-value code ("N/A") used throughout the dataset. File_Manifest_BD_Forage2Season.xlsx — a manifest listing every file referenced by the tabular dataset (VIS–NIR spectral replicates, RGB and thermal imagery, UAV multispectral orthomosaics, and Sentinel-2 products), organized by category with file counts and relative paths. Dataset Structure The master file BD_Forage2Season.xlsx contains 400 rows × 107 columns, organized into the following variable groups: Identification and Geospatial Information (12 columns)Sampling date, season, regrowth day, tussock location, light condition, tussock identifier, and geographic coordinates in WGS84 format (degrees, minutes, seconds). Morphological and Structural Variables (5 columns)Number of stems, number of leaves, tussock height (cm), measurement height, and canopy angle. VIS–NIR Proximal Spectral Variables (44 columns)Vegetation indices and spectral variables derived from proximal VIS–NIR measurements: NDVI, GNDVI, NDRE, SRI, TVI, SAVI, OSAVI, ARVI, SARVI, SARVI2, EVI2, NLI, VARI, CLGR, CLRE, NDWI, RDVI, WDRVI, NGRVI, GRVI, LAI, ARI1, ARI2, BGI, BRI, NPCI, NPQI, PSRI, and SIPI. The dataset also includes calibrated spectral reflectance values for NIR, Red, Green, Blue, and RedEdge bands, maximum reflectance, logarithmic spectral transformations, and first derivative spectral features. Within this group, the five key-wavelength reflectance values and the spectral maximum constitute raw sensor output, while the log-transformed bands, the red-edge derivative, and the 29 vegetation indices are derived/processed products computed from that raw reflectance data (see Data_Dictionary for the per-column breakdown). Four replicate spectra were collected per tussock (40) per sampling date (10), using a calibrated VIS–NIR spectrometer referenced with a Spectralon diffuse reflectance standard. RGB-Derived Canopy Metrics and Covariance Features (14 columns)Variables extracted from RGB image segmentation using a Mahalanobis distance-based methodology implemented in Python (numpy, scipy; Python 3.12). Reference pixels for the covariance matrix were manually sampled from a single representative leaf per tussock. Includes: green pixel fraction, mean green value, Mahalanobis deviation metrics, Mahalanobis distance, pixel count, greenness classification, Boolean canopy cover indicators, and covariance features derived from R, G, B, RedEdge, and NIR channels. Environmental Microclimate Variables (4 columns)Relative humidity (%), solar radiation, precipitation (mm), and ambient temperature (°C). These variables are recorded once per sampling date and shared across all tussocks measured on that date. Biomass and Nutritional Quality Variables (14 columns)Fresh biomass, dry biomass subsamples, dry matter production, dry matter percentage, and laboratory-derived nutritional parameters: crude protein (CP), crude fiber (CF), neutral detergent fiber (NDF), acid detergent fiber (ADF), ether extract (EE), ash (ASH), and lignin (LIG). Also includes biomass classification categories. Imagery and File Path References (14 columns)Structured file paths linking each observation with associated sensing products: four VIS–NIR spectral replicate files, RGB tussock imagery, thermal imagery, UAV multispectral orthomosaics (Green, Red, RedEdge, NIR, NDVI), and Sentinel-2 VIS and NDVI products (available for only 2 of the 10 sampling dates — see below). See File_Manifest_BD_Forage2Season.xlsx for the complete list of files referenced by these columns. Morphological, spectral, imagery, and biomass (fresh/dry weight) variables are recorded independently for each of the 400 tussock-date observations. The seven forage nutritional-quality parameters (CF, NDF, ADF, LIG, CP, EE, ASH), by contrast, were derived from 40 group-level composite laboratory samples — one per tussock, pooling biomass across its sampling dates — and the same composite value is repeated across the rows corresponding to that tussock. Users should therefore treat the nutritional-quality columns as tussock-level (n = 40), not as 400 independent replicates, when conducting statistical analyses. Environmental/microclimate variables are recorded per sampling date and shared across all tussocks measured on that date (n = 10 independent values). Complementary Files RGB Imagery — High-resolution tussock images acquired using an Apple iPhone 15 (48 MP). Thermal Imagery — Thermal images acquired using a FLIR 300 long-wave infrared sensor (7.5–14 µm). UAV Multispectral Orthomosaics — Radiometrically calibrated (Spectralon reference) GeoTIFF orthomosaics generated from flights performed with a DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral at approximately 50 m altitude, including Green, Red, RedEdge, NIR, and NDVI products. Ten unique UAV flight acquisitions were performed, one per sampling date, covering the 21 full-sun tussocks (imagery is not applicable to shaded tussocks, which are not attributable at the landscape level). VIS–NIR Spectral Data — Forty folders containing replicate spectral measurements stored as .txt files for each tussock and sampling date. Sentinel-2 Imagery — Data Availability and ProcessingSentinel-2 Level-2A products are delivered pre-calibrated radiometrically and atmospherically corrected by the data provider (Sen2Cor L2A processing). Scenes with cloud cover below 30% were evaluated for the study area and the ten field-observation dates. Suitable Sentinel-2 imagery meeting the spatial, temporal, and cloud-coverage criteria was available for only 2 of the 10 field-observation dates (2024-08-16 and 2024-08-23). The Excel dataset identifies the Sentinel-2 image associated with the corresponding observations for these two dates only; the remaining eight dates are coded as "N/A" in the plot-Sentinel2-VIS and plot-Sentinel2-NDVI columns, as no suitable acquisition was available within the defined temporal criteria. The available Sentinel-2 files provided in this dataset correspond to processed PNG visualizations generated from the original Level-2A imagery and are therefore classified as processed products, not raw Sentinel-2 data. UAV imagery is available for 210 of the 400 observations (the 21 full-sun tussocks across all 10 sampling dates). Missing observations were primarily associated with tropical cloud cover and adverse weather conditions, or with tussocks under shade canopy for which landscape-level imagery is not attributable. Missing values within the dataset are coded as "N/A". INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Protected agriculture across the Americas ranges from high-technology greenhouses in North America to lower-cost protected systems in Latin America, yet both depend heavily on water, nutrients, energy, and synthetic materials. These technological and regional contrasts create unequal capacities to implement circular production models. This study aimed to characterize the evolution, collaboration patterns, conceptual structure, and research gaps of circular economy applications in protected agriculture across the Americas. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework, 144 Scopus-indexed documents published between 1996 and 2025 were analyzed using VOSviewer version 1.6.20, and the Bibliometrix R package version 5.4.1. Performance indicators, co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic mapping were examined. The annual growth rate of 12.57% and an international co-authorship rate of 44.03% indicate an expanding and increasingly collaborative field; however, production remained concentrated in the United States, Brazil, and Mexico. The conceptual structure was dominated by hydroponics, aquaponics, nutrient recycling, wastewater management, and water quality, showing that circularity has been operationalized mainly through water and nutrient loops. The thematic structure highlights connections among production technologies, water treatment, and nutrient management. The studies discussed illustrate advances in these areas and identify the need to evaluate resource recovery alongside crop performance, microbiological quality, energy requirements, and environmental impacts. Thus, the regional research agenda should prioritize these thematic gaps while strengthening collaboration with countries that remain weakly represented. These priorities can guide funding and coordinated research toward circular strategies adapted to the technological diversity of protected agriculture in the Americas.

AUTORES: Joan Fernando Díaz-Calderon; Dubert Yamil Cañar-Serna; Eliana Martínez Pachón
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Peasants in the Valle del Cauca region of south-western Colombia have established agroecology as an alternative model to the agricultural modernization driven by the sugarcane agro-industry, drawing on long-standing agroecological peasant schools, model farms, and active participation in social movements defending the peasantry. This study aimed to understand the motivations behind agroecological transitions, the practices implemented, and the bottlenecks hindering their adoption, addressing a gap in the quantitative methodologies proposed for evaluating the performance of agroecological production units. We mapped agroecological experiences and conducted 19 semi-structured interviews with participants from 12 peasant organizations, complemented by direct measurements such as soil structure, and analyzed narratives using lexical analysis framed by the HLPE’s 13 agroecological principles. Results showed that 69% of narratives were organized around social aspects, highlighting peasant experimentation, the importance of model farms, knowledge exchanges, institutional support in disseminating input-substitution practices, and communities’ active participation in political processes defending the peasantry and the territory as key drivers of agroecological territorialization. The main obstacles to agroecological adoption were structural rather than technical: limited access to fair markets, certification schemes, and credit; land tenure insecurity and territorial conflicts; and continued dependence on commercial seeds and synthetic inputs. This qualitative, narrative-based approach offers a way to capture producers’ experiences and meanings complementing rather than replacing quantitative methodologies, recognizing producers’ knowledge and agency.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad del Magdalena, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Las cadenas agroalimentarias contribuyen de manera significativa con las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero (GEI) y, en consecuencia, con el calentamiento global. En las cadenas de valor lácteas, el metano entérico (CH₄), generado durante la fermentación ruminal, constituye una de las principales fuentes de emisión en términos de carbono equivalente (CO₂ eq), especialmente en sistemas lecheros tropicales, donde la heterogeneidad de la dieta, el manejo y las condiciones productivas incrementa la incertidumbre de su estimación. En muchos casos, esta incertidumbre se relaciona con el uso de factores de emisión genéricos y con la limitada representatividad de los datos empleados en los inventarios de GEI. En este contexto, la cadena de suministro del queso costeño representa un sistema agroalimentario de particular interés por su relevancia económica, territorial y cultural en regiones tropicales del Caribe colombiano. Esta cadena comprende los eslabones de producción primaria de leche, transformación, comercialización y consumo final, cada uno con procesos y flujos que inciden en el desempeño ambiental del producto. Sin embargo, la cuantificación de su huella de carbono todavía presenta limitaciones metodológicas, particularmente por la escasa integración de información específica sobre el animal, la dieta y el manejo productivo en la estimación del CH₄ entérico, lo cual restringe la precisión de los resultados y la identificación de puntos críticos de emisión. Frente a esta problemática, el presente estudio propone el desarrollo de un marco metodológico para la estimación del metano entérico y su integración en la huella de carbono de la cadena de suministro del queso costeño en sistemas lecheros tropicales. El enfoque combina la modelación mecanicista mediante el sistema de Carbohidratos y Proteínas Netos de Cornell (CNCPS) con el análisis de ciclo de vida (ACV), con el propósito de mejorar la representatividad de la estimación de emisiones y su incorporación en la evaluación ambiental del sistema. A diferencia de enfoques convencionales, como Tier 2 del IPCC, el uso del CNCPS permite una mayor sensibilidad a las condiciones locales, al considerar de forma más explícita la interacción entre la composición de la dieta, la fisiología ruminal y el desempeño animal. Por su parte, el ACV se emplea para cuantificar los impactos ambientales, que están asociados a los GEI que se producen en la cadena de suministro del queso costeño. La estructura metodológica del estudio se fundamenta en los lineamientos de las normas ISO 14040 e ISO 14044 para análisis de ciclo de vida, en la ISO 14067 para huella de carbono de producto y en el estándar de la Federación Internacional de Lechería (IDF, 2022), lo que favorece la consistencia, trazabilidad y comparabilidad de los resultados. En conjunto, el marco metodológico propuesto busca fortalecer la estimación del CH₄ entérico en sistemas lecheros tropicales y mejorar su integración en estudios de huella de carbono aplicados a productos lácteos tradicionales. Se espera que este enfoque contribuya a identificar puntos críticos de emisión, reducir incertidumbres metodológicas y generar insumos técnico-científicos para el diseño de estrategias de mitigación orientadas a la sostenibilidad ambiental de la cadena de suministro del queso costeño. Metodológicamente, el estudio se estructura en cuatro etapas. En primer lugar, se realizará la delimitación del sistema y la caracterización de los eslabones que integran la cadena de suministro del queso costeño, identificando procesos, entradas, salidas y fuentes potenciales de emisión. En segundo lugar, se recopilará información productiva, nutricional y de manejo del sistema lechero tropical, incluyendo variables asociadas al animal, la dieta y el desempeño productivo, que servirán de base para la estimación del CH₄ entérico mediante el modelo CNCPS. En tercer lugar, las emisiones entéricas obtenidas se incorporarán al inventario del ACV, junto con las emisiones derivadas del uso de insumos, energía, transporte, transformación y comercialización, con el fin de estimar la huella de carbono del queso costeño bajo un enfoque de “cuna al consumidor”.

AUTORES: Orlando Velázquez; Victoria Escobar; Fabrice Eric Vaillant; Misael Cortes; Pablo Emilio Rodríguez
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement, Université de Montpellier, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Institut de Recherche pour le Développement, UMR QualiSud
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Flash vacuum expansion is an emerging thermophysical technology that combines rapid fruit heating with instantaneous decompression in a vacuum chamber to obtain high-quality purees. To date, this technology has been mainly studied in batch systems, with limited evidence regarding its application in small and medium-scale agro-industries. This study evaluated the technical performance and techno-economic feasibility of a continuous flash vacuum expansion process for the production of Andean blackberry puree. A 2 × 2 factorial design was applied, testing two heating times (48 and 67 s) and two feed rates (4 and 6 kg·min⁻¹). Heat transfer was modeled using a transient conduction–convection approach with temperature-dependent properties. Product analyses included microbial inactivation, retention of cyanidins, ellagitannins, and ascorbic acid (UHPLC-DAD), as well as the evaluation of texture, color, and sensory attributes. The optimal condition (48 s, 6 kg·min⁻¹) achieved a 72% yield, a 7-log microbial reduction, and a 77% increase in cyanidin content compared with the untreated puree. Ellagitannins, ascorbic acid, and sensory attributes were preserved, confirming the high functional quality of the product. Economic projections over 15 years indicated a payback period of approximately two years and an internal rate of return of 93%, surpassing values commonly reported for conventional fruit-processing technologies. These results demonstrate, for the first time, that continuous flash vacuum expansion at industrial scale ensures microbial safety, enhances bioactive compound retention, and represents a technically and economically viable alternative for small and medium-scale agro-industries.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Universidad Nacional Abierta y a Distancia, Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement, UMR QualiSud
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) supports coastal value chains, yet compositional variation across varieties and production landscapes remains insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated physical, physicochemical, mineral, and metabolic variation across two coastal landscape types (alluvial and fluviomarine plains) and three coconut varieties (Manila Red, Hybrid, and Alto Pacífico) using a 2 × 3 factorial sampling design ( n = 36 biological replicates; each replicate comprising six fruits from six different palms). Coconut water was analyzed for pH, titratable acidity, soluble solids, and mineral composition; kernel physical characteristics, moisture, and total oil content (dry basis) were determined; and coconut milk was characterized physicochemically and profiled by untargeted UPLC–ESI–QTOF–MS. Kernel circumference differed among varieties ( p = 1.21 × 10 −6 ), and the kernel-to-water ratio differed between landscapes ( p = 0.0401), whereas no significant landscape, variety, or interaction effects were detected for kernel moisture, total oil content, or the evaluated coconut-water and coconut-milk physicochemical characteristics. Mineral composition showed analyte-specific variation: Ca was associated with variety ( p = 1.04 × 10 −4 ), whereas Mg and K exhibited significant variety × landscape interactions ( p = 4.88 × 10 −7 and p = 0.00214, respectively). Untargeted metabolomics retained 709 features after QC filtering; PCA showed no evident clustering by landscape or variety, and no valid PLS-DA model was obtained. Overall, variation was trait-specific, with limited detectable effects for most physicochemical characteristics and more pronounced variation in coconut-water mineral composition.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Afro-descendant communities in Colombia, settled in swamp ecosystems, live with complex socio-economic dynamics such as a lack of access to land and poverty. This represents the greatest threat to the food sovereignty of these populations. The objective of this research was to evaluate the sustainability of the agro-food system of the Afro-descendant community Amada Cabas Gutiérrez, settled in the Zapatosa swamp in Colombia. A methodology based on sustainability indicators was used with the participation of 20 families, following three phases: (1) participatory characterisation of the agro-food system, (2) construction of the analysis framework and definition of indicators, and (3) on-site sustainability assessment. Socio-economic potentials around food exchange practices were identified. Training in the construction of the community life plan and access to productive land were identified as a priority need. The need to generate spaces for intergenerational encounters around food, food production and the agro-pastoral way of life was highlighted.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This study maps research on energy, exergy, environmental, and economic assessment of solar agricultural drying systems using 145 Scopus-indexed documents published from 2003 to 2025. A broad search returned 917 records; addition of an explicit 4E/LCA block reduced the set to 155, and title-and-abstract screening retained 145 documents. The bibliometric corpus comprises 127 core and 18 contextual records. Full-counting analysis of author keywords retained 33 terms at a minimum occurrence of three, producing 178 links and a network density of 0.337. Of the 127 core records, 87 addressed energy, 105 exergy, 52 environmental performance, and 51 economics; only 23 integrated all four dimensions and 10 explicitly applied life cycle assessment. Energy–exergy was the strongest pairwise overlap (Jaccard = 0.587), followed by environment–economics (0.471). Indirect and mixed-mode configurations showed broader multi-dimensional coverage than direct or greenhouse configurations, while thermal storage/phase-change materials and PV/PVT were the most frequent integration niches. The field has expanded rapidly since 2020 but remains geographically concentrated and methodologically uneven. The evidence therefore supports partial convergence toward 4E assessment rather than a mature or dominant integrated paradigm.

AUTORES: Jahir O. Vargas-Domínguez; Jorge Noriega; Yolanda Gómez Vargas; Diego Ortiz Ortega; Nathalia M. Correa‐Valencia
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad de Antioquia, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Enzootic bovine leukosis, paratuberculosis, and bovine tuberculosis are chronic infectious diseases with important implications for dairy productivity and animal health. Evidence integrating the three agents into the same animals is scarce in tropical highland dairy systems and almost absent for herds enrolled in official bovine tuberculosis certification programs. An analytical observational study evaluated 733 cattle from 37 specialized dairy herds in a highland dairy region of Colombia using serological (ELISA) and molecular methods (qPCR, ddPCR) to detect bovine leukemia virus (BLV), Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP), and Mycobacterium bovis. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a random intercept for herds accounted for the clustering of animals within herds, and agreement between diagnostic tests was quantified using Cohen's kappa. At the herd level, BLV was detected in 70.3% of the herds by ddPCR and 67.6% by ELISA, MAP was detected in 27.0% by ELISA and 18.9% by fecal qPCR, and M. bovis was not detected in any herd. At the animal level, BLV proviral DNA was detected in 34.8% of the cattle, and BLV antibodies were detected in 31.9%; MAP fecal DNA was detected in 1.2%, and MAP antibodies were detected in 1.9%, and no animal tested positive for M. bovis by any method. Agreement between the two BLV definitions was substantial (kappa = 0.79), whereas the two MAP definitions identified essentially nonoverlapping animals (kappa = 0.07). The odds of MAP fecal shedding did not differ between BLV-positive and BLV-negative animals, but the estimate was imprecise and compatible with a wide range of effects (OR = 0.26; 95% CI: 0.03-2.43; p = 0.24, from the mixed-effects model), reflecting only nine MAP-positive animals and a single coinfected animal. Age was associated with BLV proviral detection in the mixed-effects model, although the association was less precise and not statistically significant when cluster-robust standard errors were used. BLV was detected in a high proportion of animals and herds, whereas MAP detection was limited, and no evidence of current M. bovis infection was detected using the diagnostic approaches applied in this selected population. The absence of a detectable BLV-MAP association does not imply biological independence, given the small number of MAP-positive animals. The marked clustering of BLV detection within herds (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.45) indicates substantial unmeasured herd-level heterogeneity and has direct implications for the design of surveillance in these systems. These findings support pathogen-specific surveillance and control strategies.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Essential oils are increasingly recognized as ecofriendly alternatives to synthetic pesticides, especially in tropical regions with high pest pressure and limited crop protection resources. This study evaluates native and naturalized plants in Guinea-Bissau— Ageratum conyzoides , Azadirachta indica , Chromolaena odorata , Cymbopogon giganteus , and Mesosphaerum suaveolens —for sustainable pest management, combining ethnobotanical documentation, essential oils characterization, and existing bioactivity data focused on cashew pests. An African-wide ethnobotanical assessment using Plant Resources of Tropical Africa (PROTA) and Scopus databases revealed that these species were predominantly used for medicinal and pest-related applications, most frequently reported in West Africa. Essential oils were extracted from leaves by hydrodistillation and chemically characterized using gas chromatography coupled with flame ionization detection and mass spectrometry. Essential oils yields varied among species; C. odorata and C. giganteus yielded the highest. Chemical profiling revealed species-specific compositions dominated by chromenes, monoterpene hydrocarbons, and sesquiterpene hydrocarbons. Major constituents included precocene I, limonene, sabinene, β-caryophyllene, and 1,8-cineole, compounds widely reported for their insecticidal, repellent, and antifeedant properties, indicating their potential for sustainable management of cashew pests in West Africa. By combining ethnobotanical knowledge with phytochemical characterization, this study highlights the untapped potential of locally available plant-derived essential oils, rooted in traditional practices, as potentially valuable resources for sustainable agriculture.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Among domesticated species, sheep ( Ovis aries ) have achieved a wide geographic distribution due to their mobility, rusticity and ability to adapt to diverse environments and climatic conditions. Here, we characterise the genome-wide diversity of >1,000 sheep representing 77 autochthonous breeds spanning North Africa to Scandinavia using high-density genotype data. To provide a large-scale assessment of population vulnerability to climate change, we combine uni- and multivariate gene-environment association analyses, and quantify the deviation of the current genomic make-up of populations from that necessary for maintaining adaptation under climate change (genomic offset). We identify precipitation as a major driver of divergent selection and identify candidate adaptive loci overlapping genes with pleiotropic roles linking renal water balance and metabolic regulation, including glucose and insulin-related pathways. This coupling of osmoregulatory and metabolic functions likely underpins adaptation to variable drought regimes and extreme, fluctuating environments. Notably, genomic offset hot spots are identified in southwestern Europe, highlighting the need for targeted management to mitigate the effects of climate change on animal welfare and production in these regions. These findings shed light on the strategies for climate adaptation in sheep and provide insights for informed breeding programmes aimed at enhancing resilience in changing climate conditions.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Black pod disease is a major threat to global cacao ( Theobroma cacao L.) production. It is caused by multiple Phytophthora species with geographic ranges from regionally restricted to pantropical, and developing resistant cultivars requires screening against the diversity of these pathogens. This study evaluated the response of 25 cacao clones to 13 isolates of P. palmivora (eight), P. megakarya (two), and P. theobromicola (three) by nonwounding inoculation of detached pods. Lesion size and lesion expansion status were evaluated 4 days after inoculation. The linear mixed model included 178 combinations among 17 clones and 12 isolates, each represented by at least two biological replicate pods. Lesion size differed among clones (F (16, 449.2) = 25.16) and among isolates (F (11, 416.0) = 32.90), and the clone by isolate interaction was significant (F (150, 465.4) = 1.72; all P < 0.001). PENTAGONA-17 had the smallest estimated marginal lesion size (9.3 mm) and fitted values of 3.8 to 16.9 mm across 11 isolates representing all three species. ARF-31, ICS-47, POUND-7, and PMCT-73 had the next four smallest estimates, whereas NA-246 had the largest (36.7 mm). Isolate estimates varied more than fourfold, from 9.6 to 42.0 mm. Despite a marginal estimate of 12.9 mm, POUND-7 had a fitted estimate of 49.2 mm with P. megakarya GH34. The probability of lesion expansion also differed among clones and isolates (both P < 0.001). Together, these findings identify candidates for further resistance evaluation and show that multi-isolate screening provides a stronger basis for selecting materials for black pod resistance breeding.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Silvopastoral systems and other tree-based land uses are increasingly promoted for soil conservation and climate-change mitigation in tropical livestock landscapes. However, their relationships with soil organic carbon (SOC), litter decomposition, and soil macrofauna remain poorly characterized in Amazonian production systems. In this single-farm case study, we assessed SOC distribution and stocks, soil bulk density (ρb), early litter decomposition, and soil macrofaunal communities across five contrasting land-use sites in the Colombian Amazonian foothills. The silvopastoral site had been established 18 months before sampling, allowing characterization of its early-stage soil conditions. Depth-stratified sampling showed pronounced SOC enrichment in the 0-10 cm layer at the silvopastoral site, which also had lower overall ρb than open pasture (1.29 vs. 1.48 g cm-3). However, SOC stocks from the independently sampled 0-30 cm profile were comparable between these sites. Cumulative litter mass loss increased during the 60-day evaluation and varied among forage species and sites, whereas C and N concentrations and C:N showed no statistically supported temporal changes. Macrofaunal organization varied among sites and soil depths; the silvopastoral site had the highest observed Shannon diversity in the 0-10 cm layer (H' = 1.14), although no site consistently showed the greatest diversity and evenness across all depths. Overall, the silvopastoral site combined favorable surface soil attributes with comparatively high upper-layer macrofaunal diversity. Given the cross-sectional design and single-site representation of each land use, these findings constitute a baseline characterization of site-specific conditions rather than evidence of changes attributable to silvopastoral establishment.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: This study analyzed the genetic parameters and trends of growth and reproductive traits in the Costeño con Cuernos (CCC) cattle breed to support selection decisions within the Genetic Improvement Program (GIP). The traits evaluated were birth weight (BW), weaning weight (WW, adjusted to 240 days), weight at 16 months (W16, adjusted to 480 days), and calving interval (CI). The dataset comprised records from animals belonging to the Animal Germplasm Bank (AGB) and the GIP populations of AGROSAVIA, located at the Turipaná and Motilonia research centers, respectively. A total of 7,959 genealogical records were analyzed using a mixed linear model for each trait. Genetic trends were estimated through linear regression of predicted breeding values on birth year. Heritability estimates ranged from 0.05 for CI to 0.29 for WW. Genetic trends in the AGB remained stable over time. In contrast, the GIP showed positive trends for WW and W16, and a decreasing trend for CI. Inbreeding coefficients remained generally stable with minor fluctuations; however, for the AGB herd, an annual increase of 0.08% was detected. These findings demonstrate measurable genetic progress within the GIP and reinforce its importance for guiding selection strategies in the CCC breed under tropical conditions.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract Aims Understanding the mechanisms of cadmium (Cd) accumulation in cacao plants is critical to mitigating health risks associated with Cd exposure through chocolate consumption. A general and genotype-specific molecular and physiological responses were characterized. Methods Seedlings of cacao genotypes PA121 and TSH660 were exposed to 0 and 10 ppm Cd in hydroponic conditions. Samples were collected at 0, 24, and 48 h (RNAseq) and at 60 days post-treatment (ICP-OES). Gene expression profiles were compared using differential gene expression (DEG) and gene ontology analyses. Gas exchange (Gs) and abscisic acid (ABA) measurements were conducted on greenhouse-grown PA121 seedlings. Results Both shared and genotype-specific changes were observed in genes associated with detoxification, ROS, and hormone metabolism, notably ABA-related genes. In leaves, the low-accumulator exhibited fewer DEGs than the high-accumulator, whereas in roots, both genotypes displayed similar expression profiles. The high-accumulating genotype exhibited fewer statistically significant expression changes in key hormone biosynthesis genes. In roots, Cd transport family genes, including ZIP/IRT and NRAMP, were downregulated. The high-accumulator genotype exhibited significant downregulation of one ZIP and one HMA5 ortholog, whereas the response of the low-accumulator genotype included upregulation of a different HMA5 ortholog. Additionally, high-accumulator seedlings exposed to 12 ppm Cd reduced Gs without significant changes in photosynthesis, while ABA concentrations increased in roots at 36 h after Cd exposure. Conclusions Together, these results support a model in which Cd induces ABA-mediated root signaling that reduces stomatal conductance and transpiration-driven mass flow, while suppressing the expression of active Cd transporters, thereby limiting Cd uptake.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: In tropical agricultural regions, accurate estimation of reference evapotranspiration (ET 0 ) remains challenging due to climatic variability, data scarcity, and limitations of empirical models such as FAO-56 Penman–Monteith. To provide the technical basis for future field-based evapotranspiration studies, this study reports the design, construction, and calibration of an automated weighing lysimeter installed at the La Libertad Research Center in Villavicencio, Colombia. The system integrates a galvanized steel tank (1 m 3 ) reconstructed with original soil horizons, an automated sprinkler irrigation system, and a monitoring module based on load cells, soil moisture sensors, a professional weather station, and real-time data transmission powered by a photovoltaic unit. Calibration was performed using incremental load–unload cycles, achieving linear response curves with R 2 > 0.99, while soil water retention curves were developed to define irrigation thresholds. The results document the successful construction and integration of the system and show highly linear load-cell responses, also the capacity to provide high-resolution measurements under equatorial conditions, this could reduce methodological uncertainties inherent to model-based approaches. The developed system provides the technical infrastructure required for future evapotranspiration monitoring and comparison with established ET 0 estimation methods. Overall, the proposed lysimeter may support future irrigation-management, water-resource assessment, and climate-smart agriculture applications in tropical regions.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The economic injury level is a well-established paradigm in pest management. The concept states that there is a pest density where the cost of damage equals the cost of the insecticide treatment, and this density is used to trigger control actions. The economic injury level thus informs decisions about the need for insecticides based on pest sampling data. However, we argue that the concept often overlooks key biological assumptions about herbivory and typically fails to incorporate the role of crop and pest phenology in optimizing pest sampling and insecticide timing. In this review, we first overview the economic injury level concept and highlight the consequences of these limiting assumptions. We then propose that phenology models that incorporate crop susceptibility and pest life stages, combined with insecticide efficacy data, can allow for better timing of pest management actions. We also suggest that pest monitoring and management decisions should focus on minimizing pest damage accumulation, rather than limiting control actions to predefined thresholds. Future research should focus on effectively leveraging crop and pest phenology models along with field sampling to guide control actions only during the key management times. While the economic injury level has been a historically important concept guiding pest management theory and practice, adapting the concept to specific crop-pest relationships can ensure more efficient use of pest control inputs.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Ralstonia solanacearum race 2, the causal agent of Moko disease, is considered one of the most significant phytosanitary threats to Musaceae production in Colombia and Latin America, given its severe economic impact due to the loss of plantations and the reduced productive capacity of affected areas. This study aimed to map soil vulnerability to Moko disease in Colombia by integrating climatic and edaphic variables, disease surveillance data for existing outbreaks, and information on Musaceae production units nationwide. Climate and soil databases at national and international levels and expert judgment methodology were used for vulnerability analyses. The results show that, considering climatic and edaphic factors, 90.83 % of the territory exhibits areas of high and very high vulnerability. However, when banana and plantain production units are included in the final vulnerability map, this figure drops to 49.91 % of the territory. A vulnerability ranking was obtained based on the potential incidence of Moko disease. Banana-producing departments such as Magdalena, Antioquia, and Valle del Cauca, as well as plantain-producing departments like Meta, Arauca, Casanare, Córdoba, Sucre, and Chocó, showed high and very high vulnerability indices, these are all representative of the main producing areas of both crops at the national level. It was also found that acids soil, with low organic carbon, poor drainage, and high temperatures and rainfall, show high levels of vulnerability to Moko under conditions of the main banana and plantain production areas of Colombia.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: ABSTRACT Ceratocystis wilt, caused by Ceratocystis cacaofunesta , and black root rot, caused by species of Dematophora , are emerging threats to cacao ( Theobroma cacao ) production in tropical regions. Because symptoms usually appear only at advanced stages of infection, early detection tools are needed to enable timely disease management. In this study, loop‐mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assays were developed and optimised for the genus‐level detection of Ceratocystis sp. and Dematophora sp. in cacao, using primer sets designed for the rRNA internal transcribed spacer (ITS) region of Ceratocystis sp. and the large subunit (LSU) of the 28S rRNA of Dematophora sp. Reaction conditions were standardised at 65°C for 45–60 min, and assay specificity and sensitivity were evaluated against a panel of cacao‐associated pathogens and host DNA, with amplification confirmed by UV fluorescence, agarose gel electrophoresis and real‐time LAMP with melting curve analysis. The LAMP assays detected as little as 0.005 ng/μL of C. cacaofunesta DNA and 0.0005 ng/μL of Dematophora pepo DNA, being approximately 1000‐fold more sensitive than endpoint PCR and showed no cross‐reaction with non‐target DNA. Pathogenicity tests on susceptible cacao genotypes (CCN‐51 for C. cacaofunesta and IMC‐67 for D. pepo ) demonstrated infection and early LAMP molecular detection of both pathogens from 4 days post‐inoculation (dpi); this was before symptom appearance, in the case of C. cacaofunesta and 10 dpi for D. pepo. These LAMP assays provide rapid, robust and sensitive tools for early diagnosis of vascular and root diseases of cacao, with potential application in nurseries and field surveillance.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: ABSTRACT Diptera (true flies) comprise one of the most diverse insect orders; however, they remain understudied in comparison with bees and probably play a far more significant role in pollination than is commonly recognized, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Although bees are often regarded as the dominant pollinators of agricultural crops, accumulating evidence demonstrates that flies contribute substantially to pollination services across a wide range of ecosystems and crops. This review synthesizes current knowledge on dipteran pollinators of crops in the Neotropical realm. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using multiple scientific databases, incorporating peer‐reviewed articles, reviews, books, book chapters, conference proceedings, and academic theses published in English, Portuguese, and Spanish. Studies were evaluated using functional definitions of pollination that emphasize pollen transfer efficiency rather than simple flower visitation. The reviewed literature documents dipteran involvement in the pollination of numerous economically important crops, including avocado, cacao, citrus, coffee, mango, and others. Families such as Syrphidae, Calliphoridae, Ceratopogonidae, and Drosophilidae emerge as key contributors to pollination for certain crops. Despite their demonstrated importance, dipteran pollinators remain poorly studied in Central America, South America, and the Caribbean, with limited taxonomic resolution and sparse experimental validation of pollination effectiveness. Addressing these gaps is critical for improving crop management, conserving biodiversity, and enhancing the resilience of pollination services under ongoing land‐use and climate change.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Abstract To know the risk of greywater reuse in agriculture, an experiment was carried out in a greenhouse, where the effects of a household detergent (0, 500, 1500 and 3000 mg∙L− 1 ) on soil physicochemical properties and physiological indicators of habanero pepper ( Capsicum chinense Jacq.) were evaluated. The effect of the detergent on the soil parameters was dependent on the dose: while a dose of 500 mg∙L− 1 reduced the redox potential (38%), that of 3000 mg∙L− 1 increased the pH (0.2 units) and the content of P (2.5 times). Most plant growth indicators and chlorophyll content were reduced at a dose of 3000 mg∙L− 1 of the detergent and at the two evaluation moments (68 and 143 days after transplanting, DAT). The greatest effects were observed at 143 DAT, with plant dry weights being more affected than the fresh weights. The detergent did not affect the midday leaf water potential, nor the stem water potential, in any of the two moments evaluated; however, a slight reduction in leaf water potential at dawn was observed at 143 DAT. In addition, a stimulatory effect of the detergent was observed in the fruit number and total fresh and dry weight at a dose of 500 mg∙L− 1 , while at 3000 mg∙L− 1 the detergent caused the opposite effect on the fruit dry weight. The plants that grew at 3000 mg∙L− 1 maintained the fruit number similar to the controls, despite the effects on plant growth.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Objetivo: analizar la cadena agroalimentaria de la yuca en Colombia y México desde un enfoque de sistemas complejos adaptativos (SCA). Metodología: estudio cualitativo basado en una revisión documental, observación participante y entrevistas a actores clave; se trianguló la evidencia para caracterizar los arreglos institucionales, actorales y productivos. Resultados: se identificaron trayectorias contrastantes. En Colombia, la cadena es más institucionalizada, con mayor articulación organizativa y diversificación productiva. En México, la configuración es incipiente y fragmentada, dominada por circuitos locales y por una menor integración institucional. La interacción entre los arreglos institucionales y los patrones de interacción condiciona la articulación del sistema y sus márgenes de adaptación. Limitaciones: evidencia principalmente cualitativa y contextual (dos casos); investigaciones futuras pueden incorporar indicadores cuantitativos de desempeño y resiliencia, y ampliar las comparaciones a escalas subnacionales y en otros países de América Latina. Conclusiones: las diferencias entre México y Colombia no son solo productivas, sino que son el resultado de configuraciones institucionales y actorales específicas, cuya interacción explica trayectorias contrastantes en articulación y adaptación. La síntesis comparativa por dimensiones analíticas ofrece una base empírica para orientar estrategias de gobernanza y fortalecer las cadenas agroalimentarias en contextos tropicales latinoamericanos.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: El cuero de sapo de la yuca (CS) ha sido considerado una enfermedad emergente en las Américas, principalmente en Colombia entre 2019–2020. Su etiología se atribuye a una infección mixta de virus y fitoplasmas, que afecta el llenado de las raíces hasta un 100 %. En Colombia, la región Caribe es la principal zona productora de yuca, especialmente los departamentos de Córdoba, Sucre y Bolívar; por lo tanto, este trabajo se estableció para determinar la distribución espacial del CS en estos departamentos y estimar su posible ocurrencia en otras zonas productoras de la región. La estimación se realizó a partir de datos de presencia o ausencia de la enfermedad en 740 plantas de yuca. Los registros positivos con sus coordenadas se utilizaron en el modelo MaxEnt mediante el análisis de variables climáticas. La enfermedad se detectó en el 64 % de las plantas muestreadas. El modelo mostró una alta validación estadística (test AUC ≥ 0,9), lo cual permite predecir los lugares de mayor riesgo para la dispersión del CS. Las zonas más vulnerables fueron aquellas con temperatura máxima del período más caliente (BIO 5 ~ 30,4 °C) y mínima del más frío (BIO 6 ~ 23,4 °C); se ubican al centro y norte de Sucre (P = 0,46–0,75), zonas de sabana y bajo Sinú en Córdoba (P = 0,26–0,45), centro y sur del Cesar (P = 0,46–0,75) y baja Guajira (P = 0,26–0,45).

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Colombia es reconocido mundialmente por la producción de café de alta calidad, siendo este cultivo uno de los pilares de su economía agrícola y un elemento central de su identidad productiva. Ante los desafíos de la variabilidad climática y la creciente demanda de Coffea canephora, se ha impulsado su evaluación en zonas no tradicionales como el departamento de Córdoba. Este estudio comparó la estructura de la macrofauna edáfica y las propiedades fisicoquímicas del suelo entre un monocultivo de café (SCC) con tres años de establecimiento y un sistema silvopastoril (SSPP) con más de 15 años de implementación en el Centro de Investigación Turipaná de AGROSAVIA, Cereté, Córdoba. Se realizaron muestreos por triplicado en dos estratos de profundidad (0–10 cm y 10–20 cm). Se registraron 344 individuos en total, sin diferencias en abundancia entre sistemas. Sin embargo, el sistema silvopastoril presentó mayor riqueza taxonómica, con 13 órdenes y 29 morfoespecies frente a seis órdenes y 13 morfoespecies en el café, diferencia respaldada por el índice de Margalef (p = 0.0475). Las variables fisicoquímicas humedad volumétrica y conductividad eléctrica fueron significativamente superiores en el silvopastoril. Los contenidos de materia orgánica fueron similares entre los dos sistemas. Los resultados constituyen un indicador preliminar favorable para la viabilidad agroecológica del café en la región, aunque se recomienda realizar evaluaciones de mediano y largo plazo para determinar la trayectoria de la biodiversidad edáfica bajo este sistema productivo.

AUTORES: Eliana Martínez Pachón; Eliana Gisela Revelo-Gómez; Andrés Pacheco Jaimes; Gissela Fernanda Guerrero Díaz
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The transition to agroecology is one of the main strategies for increasing the sustainability of peasant, family, ethnic, and community agriculture in Colombia. However, it is unclear to what extent farmers have adopted the elements of agroecology. This study characterized the agroecological transition of 145 family farm units (FFU) in the southwestern Colombian Andes, using FAO’s Tool for Agroecology Performance Evaluation (TAPE). Agroecological adoption among family farmers units averages 47%, with coffee producers leading at 60%. Low adoption is linked to limited nutrient recycling, seed use, and high external input dependence. Additionally, we identified three types of producers based on their production systems: coffee producers located in temperate climates, and vegetable and livestock-potato producers both located in cold climates. Coffee producers exhibit the highest levels of transition because they have a platform for co-creating agroecology knowledge and have adopted, to a greater extent, ecological practices in their production units. To accelerate the agroecological transition, several actions can be implemented, including promoting peasant schools for the dissemination of agroecological practices and generating political advocacy. Likewise, implementing support programs for organizations that allow them to invest in access to land, infrastructure, equipment, and technologies necessary to improve their sustainability.

INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Autónoma de Santo Domingo, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Chili pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) production is constrained by low-fertility soils, inadequate agronomic management, and biotic and abiotic stress. This study evaluated the ef fect of chemical and organic fertilization on the growth, yield, and profitability of the Cubanela chili pepper variety under sandy loam soil conditions in Los Cajuiles, Santiago Rodríguez, Dominican Republic, during 2022–2023. A randomized complete block design with three treatments and five replications was used: an untreated control, chemical fertilization (15-15-15) and organic fertilization with humic acid. Growth, yield, and economic variables were analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Tukey’s test at the 95% confidence level. Chemical fertilization significantly enhanced vegetative and reproductive development, resulting in plants 84 cm tall, stem diameters of 11.1 mm, a greater number of flowers and fruits per plant, and longer (103 mm) and heavier (31.66 g) fruits. Total yield was highest under chemical fertilization (19 615 kg ha-1), followed by organic fertilization (13 819 kg ha-1) and the control (9 067 kg ha-1). Organic fertilization also improved growth and yield compared with the control, demonstrating its potential as a sustainable management strategy, although its ef fects were less pronounced than those of chemical fertilization. The highest benefit-cost ratio was obtained with chemical fertilization (US$5.01 per dollar invested), followed by organic fertilization (US$4.39 per dollar invested) and the control (US$1.39 per dollar invested), reflecting the greater productive and economic ef ficiency of mineral fertilization under the conditions evaluated. These results indicate that chemical fertilization maximizes the yield and profitability of Cubanela chili pepper grown on low-fertility soils, whereas organic fertilization with humic acid represents a viable alternative for production systems seeking greater sustainability without substantially reducing crop competitiveness.

AUTORES: D. Soares; Nicolas Baleret; D. Parra; Cécile Martin; Donato Andueza
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: University of Lisbon, Université Clermont Auvergne, Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement, VetAgro Sup, Unité Mixte de Recherche sur les Herbivores, Centro de Investigação Interdisciplinar em Sanidade Animal, Universidade Técnica de Lisboa, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Current methods used to measure methane ( CH 4 ) emissions from individual ruminants are difficult to apply on farms. Alternative techniques, particularly spectroscopic methods, offer a strong potential to predict individual CH 4 emissions across diverse ruminants under farm conditions. The aims of this work were to i) evaluate the potential of faecal NIRS to detect the effects of 3-nitrooxypropanol ( 3-NOP ) as antimethanogenic additive to dairy cows’ diets in comparison with milk mid-infrared ( MIR ) spectroscopy and ii) test preliminary models of CH 4 emissions from faecal NIRS of cows supplemented or not with 3-NOP. This work was based on two previous in vivo experiments conducted under controlled conditions in dairy cows (n = 43 in total) fed different diets, which evaluated the effect of 3-NOP (60 mg/kg DM) on CH 4 emissions. Individual data on CH 4 were acquired using GreenFeed (Experiment 1) or respiration chambers (Experiment 2). Individual milk and faecal samples for MIR spectroscopy and NIRS analyses, respectively, were collected during the same week of CH 4 measurement. Observed CH 4 emissions (g/day) were significantly ( P < 0.01) lower by 32% and 23% in cows fed 3-NOP-supplemented diets in Experiments 1 and 2, respectively. Milk MIR spectra did not detect cows fed with or without 3-NOP, whereas faecal NIRS did. When an existing local NIRS model for predicting CH 4 emissions was applied to faecal spectra from Experiment 1, the predicted values for 3-NOP spectra did not align with the observed measurements. The root mean square error of prediction was 174.7 g/day for the 3-NOP treatment and 75.7 g/day for the control treatment. These values were mainly explained by the bias (160.9 vs -3.9 g/day, for the 3-NOP and control treatments, respectively). To improve the CH 4 emission prediction of 3-NOP treatment, a specific exploratory prediction model was developed post-hoc for 3-NOP faecal samples in each experiment. The R 2 values and the root mean square errors of cross-validation were 0.7 and 21.7 g/day for Experiments 1 and 2, respectively. This preliminary work suggests the potential of faecal NIRS to predict CH 4 emissions from dairy cows fed diets supplemented with 3-NOP when using specific models. Further work is needed to confirm this proof of concept, calibrate specific models with additional 3-NOP data, and extend this approach to other antimethanogenic additives in future on-farm applications.

AUTORES: Óscar Iván Monsalve Camacho; Nadia Yurany Luque Sanabria; Luz Angela Sanchez-Rodriguez
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Universidad de Ciencias Aplicadas y Ambientales
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The use of substrate mixtures in soilless culture systems requires a comprehensive understanding of their chemical behavior, particularly regarding their capacity to supply or retain nutrients. This study evaluated the soluble and exchangeable fractions of coconut coir substrate mixed at five different proportions (100-0%, 75-25%, 50-50%, 25-75%, and 0-100%) with five mineral materials: coal slag, perlite, pumice, vermiculite, and zeolite. A total of 25 treatments were assessed under greenhouse conditions using carnation cuttings (Dianthus caryophyllus cv. Pomodoro) as a plant bioindicator. Results showed that vermiculite mixtures exhibited the highest cation exchange capacity (CEC) and significant sodium, manganese, and iron concentrations, while zeolite showed elevated levels of calcium and sodium in the exchangeable phase. Root development was positively correlated with soluble potassium, sodium, chloride, and sulfate levels. Treatments with equal proportions of vermiculite or pumice and coconut substrate (50:50) achieved the best rooting performance. These results highlight the importance of considering both soluble and exchangeable nutrient fractions to support substrate selection and fertigation management decisions in sustainable soilless crop production.

AUTORES: Margareth Santander; Fabrice Eric Vaillant; Augusta Caligiani; Renaud Boulanger; Martha Eugenia Londoño Zuluaga; Laura Leguizamón; Isabelle Maraval; Jader Rodríguez; Sandra Llano; Luca Calani; Andrea Fuso; Hugo A. Martínez‐Correa; Sebastián Escobar
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Centre de Coopération Internationale en Recherche Agronomique pour le Développement, UMR QualiSud, University of Parma, Universidad Nacional de Colombia
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Controlled fermentation in stirred-tank bioreactors was investigated as a strategy to modulate flavour-related metabolites and chocolate quality in cacao. The effects of temperature regime, pH adjustment, and oxygen availability regulated through mechanical agitation were evaluated using targeted metabolomic and peptidomic analyses of fermented beans, complemented by descriptive sensory analysis of chocolates. Processing conditions significantly influenced the formation of reducing sugars, peptides, organic acids, phenolic compounds, and methylxanthines, which in turn governed flavour expression. Fermentation at a constant 45 °C without pH adjustment promoted slower internal acidification, enhanced accumulation of reducing sugars and discriminating peptides, and facilitated degradation of phenolic compounds and methylxanthines, yielding chocolates characterised by balanced profiles with pronounced fruity, floral, nutty, and woody attributes and reduced bitterness and astringency. Eleven peptides were identified as potential quality markers and showed strong correlations with desirable sensory traits. In contrast, pH adjustment accelerated acidification and generated less balanced flavour profiles. These findings highlight the potential of controlled stirred-tank bioreactor fermentation as a technological platform for modulating flavour-related metabolite formation and directing cacao quality attributes through precise control of key fermentation variables.

AUTORES: Liliana Zuluaga Zuluaga; Jaime Andrés Arias Rojas
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Los bosques secos tropicales (BST) del Caribe colombiano constituyen uno de los ecosistemas más amenazados y menos estudiados del país, afectados históricamente por la deforestación, la ganadería extensiva y la expansión agrícola, lo que ha reducido drásticamente su cobertura original y ha puesto en riesgo su biodiversidad; en este contexto, el presente estudio evaluó la diversidad alfa y beta de la comunidad vegetal en 353 ha distribuidas en siete relictos de bosque seco tropical (RB) del municipio de El Carmen de Bolívar, Caribe colombiano, con el objetivo de caracterizar la composición y diversidad florística de brinzales, latizales y fustales, para lo cual se establecieron parcelas temporales de muestreo de 1000 m², registrando variables dendrométricas como la altura total y la altura de reiteración; se identificaron 67 especies pertenecientes a 30 familias, y el índice de Margalef presentó valores entre 0,25 y 7,21 en brinzales y latizales, siendo Diphysa carthagenensis y Pseudalbizzia niopoides las especies con mayor número de individuos registrados, mientras que el índice de Shannon osciló entre 0,08 y 3,25 y el de Simpson entre 0,16 y 0,95, evidenciando una diversidad alta y relativamente homogénea entre los tres estratos, sin diferencias estadísticamente significativas entre ellos para Margalef (p = 0,7003), Shannon (p = 0,9736) y Simpson (p = 0,759), lo que confirma una composición florística similar a lo largo del gradiente estructural; en diversidad beta, el índice de Sørensen registró valores entre 12 % y 100 %, mostrando alta similitud florística entre varios pares de relictos, mientras que el índice de Jaccard varió entre 5,66 % y 33,33 %, identificando a RB_4–RB_5 como el par de mayor similitud; estos resultados amplían el conocimiento sobre la diversidad florística del BST caribeño y resaltan la necesidad de fortalecer estrategias de conservación frente a las crecientes presiones antrópicas.

AUTORES: Isabel Moreno; Denys Yohana Mora-Herrera
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Universidad del Valle
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Introduction: pineapple cultivation generates large amounts of residual biomass. Consequently, the expansion of the cultivated area in Colombia requires valorization alternatives based on circular bioeconomy strategies to mitigate the environmental and health impacts associated with conventional crop residues management practices.Objective: to analyze the potential for utilizing pineapple crop residues in Colombia, particularly leaves, from three complementary perspectives: biomass availability, technological opportunities and the market potential of pineapple leaf fibre (PALF).Methodology: the theoretical availability of residual biomass was estimated using crop residue generation coefficients, cultivated area, and production statistics for the main pineapple-producing departments in Colombia. A bibliometric analysis using the Scopus database permitted the characterizing of PALF market potential using international trade statistics and sectoral market reports. Finally, the information was integrated into a SWOT analysis, and a conceptual PALF value chain was proposed.Results: Colombia was estimated to generate between 5.9 and 7.1 million tons of theoretical residual biomass in 2024. The technological review showed that vegetal fibre production for polymer composites, textiles and paper represents the most promising technical and economic valorization pathway. Market analysis identified growing opportunities associated with increasing demand for sustainable materials, while also challenges related to production costs, technical standardization, access to international markets, and limited articulation of PALF value chain in Colombia.Conclusion: pineapple crop residues in Colombia represent a valuable resource for PALF production within a circular bioeconomy framework. This study provides technical, technological, and market evidence, together with conceptual guidance for the development of the PALF value chain.

AUTORES: Paola Vanessa Sierra Baquero; Sílvia Catarino; Gonçalo J. Costa; Zinha Correia; Maria Rosa Ferreira; Elsa Borges da Silva; María Cristina Duarte; Maria Manuel Romeiras; Edgar Herney Varón-Devia; Luís Catarino; Filipa Monteiro
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: University of Lisbon, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Laboratório Associado TERRA, Museu Nacional de História Natural e da Ciência
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Cashew is an important crop in Guinea-Bissau (West Africa); however, its productivity is hindered by insect pests. This study aimed to characterize insect pests’ diversity in cashew plantations and analyze environmental factors influencing their spatial distribution across the country. Field surveys across three agroecological zones and eight administrative regions recorded biotic factors (age of the older trees and tree density), and pest occurrence, while environmental variables (temperature, precipitation, wind speed, humidity and distance to the coast) were sourced from online databases. Data analysis focused on pest characterization, assessing insect diversity, and modeling environmental drivers across the country. The study identified 13 pest morphospecies across seven orders and 12 families. Three morphospecies (ms.1 – Coccidae, ms.2 – Pseudococcidae, ms.3 – Aphididae) were assigned to the reproductive pest guild, as they infest and damage inflorescences, nuts and apples, while the non-reproductive guild had the highest relative occurrences (93%) and diversity (Shannon index: 1.05). Overall, termites exhibited the highest frequency of occurrence (69%) across 151 surveyed plantations. Among the agroecological zones, the North had the highest relative occurrence of morphospecies (49%), whereas the East had the lowest (13%). Distinct environmental drivers influence pest diversity across zones, with precipitation-related factors being primary drivers in the East, particularly precipitation seasonality, although the North and South exhibited stronger support for models including only the spatial smooth term, suggesting that pest diversity in these zones may be shaped by additional spatially structured factors not measured in our study (e.g. environmental: soil characteristics; biotic: natural enemies’ presence; anthropogenic: human settlement proximity). Biotic factors measured in our study (e.g., tree density and the age of the older trees) were not identified as significant predictors influencing pest diversity in our models. These findings highlight the need for region-specific pest management strategies tailored to the unique climatic and ecological conditions of Guinea-Bissau.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: El suelo es un sistema autoorganizado en tiempo y espacio, es la patria donde nacemos y crecemos, y la base de la vida económica y desarrollo de la humanidad. Sirve como insumo para el desarrollo industrial, soporte de edificaciones y facilitaciones para las actividades humanas. Es el medio de nutrición de cultivos y la base de la rentabilidad agrícola, formando parte esencial del desarrollo de los países como sustento agropecuario, infraestructura industrial, transporte y comercio. Además, actúa positivamente sobre el ambiente al funcionar como esponja para retener agua y contaminantes. En ese sentido, es crucial conocer sus funciones y su importancia. La revisión busca aumentar el conocimiento sobre el suelo, especialmente en América Latina y el Caribe, para fortalecer la conciencia y el cuidado de este recurso vital.

AUTORES: Ginna Natalia Cruz Castiblanco; Luisa Fernanda Saray Culma; José Luis Tauta Muñoz; Bellanid Huertas Carranza; Eduar Yovany Antolinez Sandoval; Gonzalo Rodríguez Borray
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: The sugarcane (Saccharum spp.) production system for panela and cane syrup in Guaviare lacks a systematic characterization to support the development of differentiated strategies for distinct producer types. This study aimed to identify producer typologies in Guaviare based on socioeconomic, productive, and agronomic variables. Using a stratified sampling approach, 61 surveys were conducted across the municipalities of Calamar, Miraflores, San José del Guaviare, and El Retorno. Socioeconomic data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while productive structure and agronomic practices were assessed through Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis based on Euclidean distance and Ward’s method to identify explanatory variables and establish producer typologies. The socioeconomic characterization revealed that producers had an average age of 53 years, low educational attainment, high economic vulnerability, limited access to credit, and low saving capacity. Three producer typologies were identified. Group I (41.7%) was characterized by intermediate technical management, partial adoption of improved technologies, block panela production, and active utilization of by-products. Group II (48.3%) was characterized by low levels of technification, limited use of fertilization and phytosanitary management practices, and production primarily oriented toward cane syrup. Group III (10.0%) comprised recently established producers with poorly defined agronomic practices and no established marketing channels. In conclusion, panela production in Guaviare is positioned between traditional production systems and technological modernization, highlighting the need for differentiated intervention strategies. Technological upgrading is recommended for Group I, strengthened technical assistance for Group II, and foundational training programs for Group III. These findings provide valuable insights for promoting the consolidation of sugarcane production for panela and cane syrup as a sustainable economic alternative for the department of Guaviare.

AUTORES: Cindy Mejía; Claudia Mesa; Juliana Gómez; Carolina na Ruiz; Eddy J. Bautista; Leyanis Mesa; Gloria Barrera
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Entomopathogenic fungi of the genus Metarhizium can degrade and penetrate the insect cuticle through the coordinated action of hydrolytic enzymes, mainly lipases, proteases, and chitinases, whose production varies according to the fungal species and fermentation conditions. These enzymes can be generated via submerged fermentation and subsequently employed to enhance the insecticidal activity of fungal conidia. This study aimed to increase protease production from Metarhizium robertsii Mt015 to strengthen biological control agents based solely on fungal biomass. The culture medium composition and physicochemical parameters were optimized using a statistical design approach. Biological activity assays were then performed using Tuta absoluta larvae as the target insect and Beauveria bassiana as the reference control, tested both alone and in combination with the protease extract. Optimization identified wheat bran, casein, and an initial pH of 8–10 as the most influential variables, achieving a 5.5-fold increase in protease activity compared to the basal medium. When the protease extract was combined with B. bassiana conidia, the mortality rate reached 78.2%, significantly higher than the 55.6% achieved with B. bassiana conidia alone. Bliss independence analysis indicated that the observed larval mortality exceeded the additive expectation (Δ = 23.3 percentage points; 95% CI: 16.7–30.0), supporting a synergistic interaction between B. bassiana and the protease extract at 0.68 U/mL. These results demonstrate that enzymatic supplementation markedly improves the insecticidal performance of entomopathogenic fungi, supporting the use of enzyme-enriched formulations as a complementary strategy to strengthen biological control agents and advance the development of next-generation biopesticides.

AUTORES: Yolanda Gómez Vargas; Jahir O. Vargas-Domínguez; Jorge Noriega; Nathalia M. Correa‐Valencia; Diego Ortiz Ortega
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA, Universidad de Antioquia
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) prevalence estimates vary widely across Colombian regions, with no prior longitudinal assessment of Colombian dairy systems across ecologic life zones. We assessed the temporal dynamics of MAP infection in Colombian cattle across 6 distinct ecologic life zones and explored age-related differences in MAP detection using combined serologic and molecular approaches. We longitudinally sampled 129 cattle from 6 municipalities in distinct Holdridge life zones. The animals were stratified by age group and sampled 3 times at 2-mo intervals during 2023 (Aug–Dec). Serum and fecal samples were tested by indirect ELISA and IS 900 real-time PCR (rtPCR), respectively. The apparent ELISA prevalence remained stable between 37.2% and 38% across sampling rounds (adjusted true prevalence = 29.9%). Seropositivity increased consistently with age, from 11.9% in animals <1-mo-old to 49% in animals ≥3-y-old. All of the fecal samples tested negative by rtPCR. No consistent seroprevalence clustering was observed across ecologic life zones on descriptive assessment, although management and host factors were not evaluated. We found longitudinal evidence of stable, age-related MAP seroprevalence across ecologic zones in Colombia, highlighting subclinical persistence and diagnostic limitations.

AUTORES: Izzy McCabe; Diego F. Rincón; David William Crowder
INSTITUCIONES_COLABORADORAS: Washington State University, Corporación Colombiana de Investigación Agropecuaria – AGROSAVIA
RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Decision-support systems for pest management rely on phenology models to predict the timing of pest life cycles as well as monitoring populations through sampling. Phenology models are regularly used to predict biological events that are important for management, such as the presence of a certain life stage targeted by pesticides. However, while monitoring data are often intuitively used by producers to estimate pest pressure and make decisions, capture data are rarely linked with phenology models to generate pest forecasts. Here, we introduce a model that adjusts phenology predictions across degree-days based on the sampling efficacy of trapping networks. Specifically, we created a simulation model to account for the delay in observed trap captures with respect to predicted phenology as a function of sampling efficacy, measured as the probability of individuals being sampled per degree-day. Results from the simulation were used to derive a functional relationship between the shape of the phenology model and probability of capture per degree-day. The model was then tested using trapping data for codling moth, Cydia pomonella , from eight orchards in western USA and Canada. We found that the overall average error in predictions decreased by over 50% when forecasting curves were adjusted for site-specific sampling efficacy. These results suggest a key difference in the shape between phenology models and observed pest captures in the field can be described through cumulative binomial delays. More broadly, our study shows that pest forecasting and resulting management decisions might be refined by adjusting model predictions to site-specific sampling profiles.

RESUMEN DE ARTÍCULO: Introduction: One effective and ecologically sustainable strategy that has emerged to enhance plant resilience to water deficits induced by drought stress is the application of plant growth-promoting microorganisms (PGPM). Despite this progress, there remains a lack of clarity in identifying the most effective microbial consortia and understanding the nutritional and metabolic processes that contribute to the drought resilience of strawberry crops. Methods: ) used for drought stress mitigation in plants. These were tested under two irrigation scenarios-well-watered and water-limited conditions, corresponding to 85% and 30% of their water holding capacity (WHC), respectively. Results: The co-inoculation of the CS1 consortium increased SDW by 38.23% compared to the control and 52.94% compared to CS2. Likewise, this consortium increased the concentrations of N, P, and K by 24.3%, 6.4%, and 25.7%, respectively, compared to the WS control. Finally, CS1 mitigated phytotoxic effects by activating flavonoid-type, fatty acids, and phenolic acid metabolites, as well as growth-regulating hormones, compared to the CS2 consortium and control plants, whose changes in specialized metabolism did not allow them to tolerate stress. Discussion: This study elucidated the molecular mechanisms by which microbial biostimulants increase drought tolerance.
